doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Banff recording with John Stowell and Don Thompson
summary: At Banff's 25th anniversary he played three standards on a late-night date with guitarist John Stowell, whom both praise.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Here’s another record I like a lot, that you did at Banff with John Stowell and Don Thompson.

Oh yeah. When they did the 25th anniversary of the clinic, they invited me back. I did two days. They had an hour – a recording studio overlooking these Rocky Mountains. I don’t remember how it happened. I think John was – oh, John and Donald were going in to record in the middle of the night. I said, “I’ll come in and play a few tracks.”
Which you – you did three. You did Milestones, You did Bye, Bye, Blackbird, and you did Nardis.
Yeah, standards, middle of the night.
That’s a nice record. I like it.
I think he’s one of the great unsung guitar players.
He’s special, very special, one of a kind, one of a kind.
I’ve known him for 40 years. He was . . .
Oh, he’s like St. Francis of Assisi.
Yeah, he’s beatific. I agree. There’s something about him that’s like a glow.
He lives in Portland, Oregon, lives cheaply, and travels all over the world.
He was a Link guy, right? He studied with Link.
Yes. That’s where I first heard Link, is the Stowells took me to Rapson’s that night. Here’s an interesting record you did of all Monk tunes for Jamey Aebersold.
